key_insight: By choosing the noise unraveling carefully, the average trajectory magic in noisy random quantum circuits can be reduced, but rare high-magic trajectories still dominate the classical simulation cost.
engineering_relevance: For stabilizer-based simulators of noisy quantum circuits, unraveling choice can lower typical cost, yet worst-case trajectory magic remains a critical bottleneck.
method: Studied quantum trajectories for Haar-random and T-doped random Clifford brickwork circuits under local dephasing noise.
Compared the canonical Pauli-jump unraveling with the full family of minimal Kraus unravelings.
Identified an optimal weak-measurement unraveling that minimizes trajectory-averaged stabilizer Rényi entropy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the optimal unraveling reduces the extensive magic density by a p-dependent factor while preserving linear scaling with system size, but the magic distribution remains broad.
watch_item: Lower average magic does not guarantee easier simulation, because a nontrivial fraction of trajectories still retain Haar-random magic and can set the overall cost.
paper_title: Magic in quantum trajectory unravelings of noisy random quantum circuits
